correctness.rationale: After j selected elements, their membership signatures partition the atoms into at most 2^j cells. Maintaining each corresponding cell either equal in size or both at least 2^{q-j} is preserved under one split by matching a small side exactly or choosing two threshold-large sides. At j=q this preserves exactly which Venn cells are empty, hence every atomic Boolean-term equality. Conversely the balanced recursive formula A_k splits x into two disjoint pieces each containing the required number of atoms and has quantifier rank ceil(log2 k), giving the sharp separator. The frozen exhaustive EF verifier agrees for n,m<=4 and q<=3.

final_claim: For finite Boolean algebras B_n and B_m in the ordinary Boolean-algebra language, agreement on all sentences of quantifier rank at most q is equivalent to min(n,2^q)=min(m,2^q); hence for 1<=n<m the least distinguishing rank is ceil(log2(n+1)).
